title: Coral and the Drop
premise: Hazel Montrose, a former aviation data analyst turned whistle-blower, lives under a rotating set of false identities after exposing a covert training program that taught a private network how to make aircraft disappear from every tracking system. When Flight 4471 vanishes mid-flight and every record of it is scrubbed within minutes, Hazel realizes the network is no longer practicing—they're operating. Hunted by the network's fixers and shadowed by an old lover now working inside the investigation, Hazel must choose between staying invisible and burning the program down, knowing the final proof is a black box only they can reach. In the end, Hazel trades their own survival for the truth, exposing the network at the cost of the name—and the life—they'd built to stay hidden.
about_author: Odile Lockridge is a former airline industry consultant who spent a decade inside the corridors she now writes about, leaving after a dispute she has never discussed publicly. She writes thrillers from a coastal town whose name she declines to confirm.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Hazel, living as 'Mara Voss' in a rented room in Rotterdam, wakes at 3 a.m. from the same nightmare and runs their morning counter-surveillance routine. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: exhaustion and hypervigilance establish the price already paid for survival.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Working a dead-end data job, Hazel notices Flight 4471 vanish from every feed mid-air, then vanish from history entirely—no booking, no radar archive, no witnesses online. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: dread curdling into recognition; only one system they know of can do this.

chapters.title: Ghost Signal
chapters.summary: Hazel pulls a fragment of raw telemetry from a hobbyist sensor network, confirming 4471 existed and descended in a controlled, deliberate pattern. Someone trained on this flight. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the sick certainty that staying invisible was always an illusion.

chapters.title: The Handler's Call
chapters.summary: A voice from Hazel's past—the network's fixer, Elias Crane—offers a trade: silence for safety, and a warning that two other whistle-blowers have recently 'emigrated.' POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: fear weaponized into temptation.

chapters.title: What Nadia Knew
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter to the incident: Hazel's colleague Nadia discovered the training program first and died in a car crash three days later. POV: Hazel, in memory. Emotional beat: grief and guilt as the engine of the loyalty-vs-truth theme.

chapters.title: The Investigator
chapters.summary: In Lisbon, investigator Tomas Reyes is assigned a missing-persons case: a passenger's family swears their daughter was on 4471, but the airline has no record. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: quiet, dogged doubt that will collide with Hazel's secret knowledge.

chapters.title: Burner Protocol
chapters.summary: Hazel reaches out to a journalist contact using dead-drop protocols, but finds the journalist's apartment cleared and their own safehouse flagged. Someone is ahead of them. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the walls of invisibility closing in.

chapters.title: An Old Flame, A New Badge
chapters.summary: Hazel's ex, Ines Carvalho, appears—now seconded to Reyes's task force. Their reunion is electric and dangerous: Ines doesn't know Hazel's real name, and Hazel can't tell her. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: love against duty, the first spark.

chapters.title: The Training Ground
chapters.summary: Hazel traces the program's origins to a decommissioned air base in the Azores where simulators once taught 'signature deletion'—making planes untraceable. POV: Hazel, with a brief Reyes interleave. Emotional beat: the scale of the conspiracy becomes real.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: Crane's team finds Hazel in Porto; a brutal chase through a fish market ends with Hazel wounded and a burner phone left behind deliberately—a message: we know where you sleep. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Confession at the Table
chapters.summary: Hazel approaches Ines under a controlled pretext and reveals a partial truth: the vanished flight, the program, Nadia. Ines must decide whether to report her. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: loyalty tested before love is even admitted.

chapters.title: Reyes's Ledger
chapters.summary: Reyes cross-references Hazel's claims with the missing passenger and finds the airline's records were edited by someone with executive access. He chooses to keep Hazel's name out of his report. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: an honest man learning the institution won't protect him.

chapters.title: The Passenger List That Isn't
chapters.summary: The team reconstructs who was aboard 4471: not victims—operators. A live exercise with a handpicked crew, including a name tied to a defense minister. POV: Reyes and Ines. Emotional beat: the conspiracy reaches the state itself.

chapters.title: Crane's Offer, Again
chapters.summary: Crane corners Hazel with the full deal: a new identity abroad in exchange for the recovered telemetry fragment—and reveals he trained alongside Hazel's brother, who still works for the network. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Black Box
chapters.summary: Hazel learns 4471's actual flight data recorder was never recovered—it's stored at the Azores base as the program's trophy proof of concept. The final evidence is a two-day window away. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: hope with a timer on it.

chapters.title: The Brother
chapters.summary: Hazel contacts their brother Daniel, begging him to walk away. Daniel, loyal to the network that gave him everything, warns them off—and tips Crane. POV: Daniel. Emotional beat: betrayal as an act of love, loyalty vs. truth inverted.

chapters.title: Ines Chooses
chapters.summary: Ines is ordered to hand over everything on the 'Voss' lead. Instead she burns her own report and meets Hazel at midnight, choosing the person over the institution. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: Storm Approach
chapters.summary: The team—Hazel, Ines, and a reluctant Reyes—plans the Azores infiltration as a storm front closes in; Crane's people are already reinforcing the base. POV: rotating. Emotional beat: the calm, cold clarity before the fall.

chapters.title: The Azores
chapters.summary: The infiltration goes wrong almost immediately; Reyes is shot covering the retreat, and Hazel reaches the recorder vault alone as Crane closes the perimeter. POV: Hazel and Reyes. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the cost of the truth.

chapters.title: Drop
chapters.summary: Hazel recovers the black box and broadcasts its contents on an open aviation frequency as Crane takes them at gunpoint—too late; the world is already listening. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: triumph and capture in the same breath.

chapters.title: Every Name at Once
chapters.summary: Hazel, in custody and traded between agencies, gives testimony under their real name for the first time in years, dismantling the network as arrests ripple across three countries. Daniel is taken quietly. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: grief, vindication, and the strange lightness of being visible.

chapters.title: Coral
chapters.summary: Months later, Hazel—no longer hiding, but never safe—meets Ines on a reef-diving trip; coral, they reflect, survives by building slowly in plain sight. The last whistle-blower's file is still out there. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, with the door left ajar.
